Article Title: 'Who ordered SIR?' Congress seeks SC nod to pose 48 questions to EC, CEC Gyanesh Kumar over 'vote chori'
Article Text:
Congress seeks clarification on how many decisions taken by the CEC had been opposed by the other two Election Commissioners.

NEW DELHI: The Congress on Monday said the Election Commission of India 's (ECI) affidavit before the Supreme Court had failed to address questions raised over alleged "Vote Chori", adding that INDIA bloc leaders now had sought the court's permission to submit an interrogatory to the poll body.In a post on X, the party said a list of 48 questions had been submitted for the Election Commission, including chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, the two Election Commissioners and the Director General of IT, to answer over alleged lapses in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls."The Election Commission of India's affidavit in the Supreme Court has not answered a single question raised on Vote Chori," Congress said.As per news agency PTI, Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi has also told the Supreme Court that the Election Commission's response failed to identify officials who authorised changes to the online version of Form 6 in connection with the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Gandhi and other petitioners have sought sworn replies from the Deputy Election Commissioner and other officials on who authorised the SIR, the exclusion of voters and the upgrades and alterations made to the Election Commission's online portal.The party has also sought clarification on how many decisions taken by the CEC had been opposed by the other two Election Commissioners.Congress alleged that lapses in the SIR exercise had paved the way for what it termed "Vote Chori" and called for the poll panel's top officials to personally respond to the questions.
Article Summary: The Congress said the Election Commission of India's affidavit before the Supreme Court had failed to address questions raised over alleged "Vote Chori" The party has now sought the court's permission to submit an interrogatory to the poll body. Congress alleged that lapses in the SIR exercise had paved the way for what it termed "VoteChori"

The BJP on Monday hit out at Congress after a video showed party leader Devendra Yadav throwing plastic bottle into the Yamuna, accusing the opposition party of attempting to pollute the river even as the government works to clean it ahead of Chhath Puja In a post on X, the BJP called Yadav's alleged act a “shameful attempt” to pollute the river and accused the Congress of disrespecting the faith of millions of Chhath devotees.“On the one hand, the BJP government is cleaning up the Yamuna and building grand ghats for Chhath devotees, while on the other, Congress is once again busy polluting the Yamuna,” the party said.“Why is cleaning up the Yamuna such a problem? Article Title: Shah hits back at Rahul, says he's defaming India at global platforms
Article Text:

PUNE:Union home minister Amit Shah Sunday accused leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi of attempting to tarnish India's image on an international platform, referring to his remarks at the Bharat Summit 2026 in Hyderabad.The Union minister was addressing a gathering at the foundation stone-laying ceremony of National Heavy Engineering Cooperative Ltd in in Pune.Referring to the Congress-organised summit in Hyderabad on Nov 13-14, Shah said, "The summit was named Bharat Summit, but Rahul expressed anti-India views at an international conference and attempted to defame India on the global platform."Shah was referring to Rahul's statement at the summit that India was no longer a democracy and that BJP was "systematically weakening" democratic institutions."I strongly condemn Rahul ji's attempt to defame India, India's development story, India's democracy and our PM on an international platform," he said, adding, "Whether it is the governing party or the opposition, or any political party, can you defame India and India's PM at an international summit?""Congress is continuously taking out its frustration in different ways after losing elections for three consecutive terms," the home minister said, adding that Rahul and Congress would not be able to form govt by criticising the country on international platforms and should instead visit villages and interact with people."If you want 'power', stop travelling abroad and start going to villages in India. Perhaps then, you may get a chance someday... People had given you an opportunity. You committed corruption and scams worth Rs 12 lakh crore. People of the country removed you from office. They made Narendra Modi the PM. In the last 12 years, no allegation of corruption has been levelled against Narendra Modi," he added.He also asked Congress workers not to follow the party leadership's approach, and warned, "Rahul Gandhi will not listen, but I want to tell Congress workers that if you continue following them in this direction, you will not get your turn for 30 years."
Article Summary: Shah was referring to Rahul's statement at the summit that India was no longer a democracy and that BJP was "systematically weakening" democratic institutions. He was addressing a gathering at the foundation stone-laying ceremony of National Heavy Engineering Cooperative Ltd in in Pune.

Article Title: 'No place for goons': CM Adhikari's warning to criminals after encounter of Shantiniketan accused
Article Text:
CM Suvendu Adhikari defends Ratan Sheikh encounter

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday warned criminals and people possessing illegal firearms to leave the state. His warning came after Ratan Sheikh, the prime accused in the Santiniketan shooting case, was killed in a police encounter in Birbhum's Nanoor.Speaking to news agency ANI, Adhikari said Sheikh had opened fire at police personnel when they attempted to arrest him. He said the police took necessary action in response."He shot at the police, and the police did what needed to be done on the spot. It would not be appropriate for me to comment on this. There is no place for goons and rapists in West Bengal," Adhikari said.Issuing a warning to criminals and those possessing illegal firearms, he added, "Even now, whatever remaining goons and those with illegal arms are left, flee from here; leave immediately. There is no place for them here."Sheikh was accused of opening fire at a police team that went to arrest him in connection with the Santiniketan shooting incident. The firing took place on Friday evening in the Layek Bazar area of Bolpur.Three police personnel had reached the area to apprehend Sheikh. However, he allegedly opened fire after spotting them, injuring constable Biswajit Das in his left leg. Sheikh fled the spot and had been absconding since the incident.Sheikh was killed in a police encounter in Nanoor on Sunday. Adhikari described him as a dreaded criminal and said 36 cases had been registered against him. Sheikh had been granted bail in a robbery case and returned to the area last Friday.Following the shooting, Adhikari visited injured constable Biswajit Das at Bardhaman Medical College and Hospital. Doctors said his condition was stable.
Article Summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari warned criminals and people possessing illegal firearms to leave the state. His warning came after Ratan Sheikh, the prime accused in the Santiniketan shooting case, was killed in a police encounter in Birbhum's Nanoor.

Article Title: TMC vs TMC: Mamata-led faction submits affidavits to EC, accuses rival group of forgery
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Mamata Banerjee-led All India Trinamool Congress on Sunday submitted affidavits and other documents to the Election Commission as part of the ongoing dispute over control of the party.Speaking to reporters after submitting the documents, TMC MP Kalyan Banerjee accused the rival faction of using police intimidation in West Bengal to procure forged affidavits for submission to the Election Commission.He alleged that police officers had forced party leaders, office-bearers and grassroots workers to sign affidavits backing the rival group, claiming that several signatures had also been forged.Kalyan Banerjee said his faction had submitted all its pleadings and affidavits in compliance with the Supreme Court's directions, providing both hard and soft copies to the poll panel."We have original affidavits. We have no fear. They have forged affidavits. So they have not given it out of fear," he said."Every police station's officer forced people to sign the affidavits, and in many affidavits, the signatures are forged," he alleged.Questioning why the rival faction had not shared copies of its affidavits with his side, Banerjee said the Election Commission could not take cognisance of documents that had not been disclosed to them.He said his faction would also send soft copies of all the affidavits it had submitted to the Ritabrata-led group."Whenever the affidavits are disclosed, we will prosecute them. We will put Mr Ritabrata Banerjee in jail," he said.Banerjee said his faction had submitted affidavits from 17 MPs, 32 MLAs in West Bengal, five MLAs in Meghalaya and one MLA in Assam, apart from more than two lakh affidavits from grassroots-level workers.He also challenged the rival faction to demonstrate its support among legislators, questioning Ritabrata Banerjee's claim that he had the backing of 65 MLAs.The poll panel is examining the dispute under the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968, which empowers it to adjudicate claims by rival factions of a recognised political party.The dispute began after a rival faction led by Ritabrata Banerjee staked its claim to the party's organisational control, election symbol and funds.
Article Summary: TMC MP Kalyan Banerjee accused rival faction of using police intimidation in West Bengal to procure forged affidavits. He alleged that police officers had forced party leaders, office-bearers and grassroots workers to sign affidavits backing the rival group.

Article Title: Punjab Congress sets up panel to vet leaders joining from other parties ahead of 2027 polls
Article Text:
File photo: Punjab Congress Chief Pargat Singh

NEW DELHI: The Punjab Congress has formed a four-member committee to oversee the induction of leaders from other political parties, with the state heading into Assembly elections early next year.The panel, constituted by state Congress president Pargat Singh on Sunday, will coordinate the process and ensure consultations with local party leaders before any new entrant is admitted.The committee includes Congress Working Committee member and former MLA Vijay Inder Singla, MLA and deputy leader of the Congress Legislature Party Aruna Chaudhary, former MLA Kushaldeep Singh Dhillon and MLA Hardev Singh Laddi.According to the office order issued by the Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee, the panel will consult senior Congress leaders from the concerned area and the respective district Congress committee presidents before inducting any leader.The order states that the induction process will proceed only after their views have been taken into consideration and coordination with the local leadership has been ensured.The committee has been constituted with immediate effect.This move comes amid Congress's bid to strengthen its organisation and expand its political base ahead of the 2027 polls. In May, several leaders and workers from the Aam Aadmi Party, Shiromani Akali Dal and BJP had joined the Congress at an induction programme in Batala. The party has also stepped up its election preparations, with its leadership recently holding discussions on candidate selection, constituency-level assessments and winnability after the AAP announced its first list of candidates.Elections to the 117-member Punjab Assembly are due early next year.
Article Summary: The Punjab Congress has formed a four-member committee to oversee the induction of leaders from other political parties. The panel will coordinate the process and ensure consultations with local party leaders before any new entrant is admitted. The move comes amid Congress's bid to strengthen its organisation and expand its political base ahead of the 2027 polls.

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke in another X post on Monday claimed that the local Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) in his hometown had “suddenly gone on leave” and that a new officer had been brought in to take charge.Dipke’s remarks came amid party's earlier claim that he and fellow CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Dass could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other provisions.AISA national president Neha Bora on Monday claimed that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station.In a post on X, Neha said "Rosy and other protesting journalists are detained at Delhi Cantt PS. Article Title: Car thief drives away with sleeping girl, drops her at Sirkazhi
Article Text:
The girl was rescued by autorickshaw drivers

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





CHENNAI: An unidentified man who stole a car near Guduvanchery in Chengalpet district on Sunday night, apparently unaware that a 12-year-old girl was sleeping inside, drove away with the child before dropping her off at the Sirkazhi new bus stand in Mayiladuthurai district early on Monday.The girl was rescued by autorickshaw drivers, while police are searching for the suspect, who fled with the vehicle.Police said the girl's father, Malaiarasan, a native of Kamuthi in Sivaganga district, was returning to his residence in Guduvanchery with his wife and daughter after visiting his hometown.During the journey, the family stopped at a cloud kitchen operated by Malaiarasan at Vallanchery near Guduvanchery to collect food. The couple stepped out of the car, leaving their daughter asleep inside. An unidentified man, who noticed the unattended vehicle, allegedly drove away with it, apparently unaware that the girl was sleeping inside.When they returned a few minutes later, they found both the car and their daughter missing. After searching the surrounding areas, Malaiarasan lodged a complaint with Guduvanchery police.Based on the complaint, police registered a case and formed three special teams to trace the girl and the vehicle.They examined CCTV footage from nearby establishments and collected details of vehicles that had passed through the area.Meanwhile, around 4.30 am on Monday, an unidentified person driving the stolen car reportedly reached the Sirkazhi new bus stand and dropped off the girl before fleeing with the vehicle.The girl approached autorickshaw drivers waiting at the bus stand and informed them that an unidentified man had taken her away in the car. The drivers immediately took her to the Sirkazhi All Women Police Station and handed her over to the police.Sirkazhi police alerted their Guduvanchery counterparts and informed the girl's parents that she had been rescued. Police said the girl was safe and that CCTV footage was being examined to trace the suspect and recover the car. Police suspect the man stole the vehicle without realising that the girl was asleep inside.
Article Summary: Unidentified man stole a car near Guduvanchery in Chengalpet district on Sunday night. He was apparently unaware that a 12-year-old girl was sleeping inside. The girl was rescued by autorickshaw drivers, while police are searching for the suspect, who fled with the vehicle.

Article Title: Mahayuti split takes centre stage as Latur DCC Bank goes to polls today
Article Text:
Latur District Central Cooperative Bank

The election to Latur District Central Cooperative Bank on Sunday has emerged as the clearest public sign yet of cracks within Mahayuti.The contest pits Congress-backed Sahakar Panel, led by former MLA and bank chairperson Dhiraj Deshmukh, against Mahayuti-backed Rayateche Raje Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Parivartan Panel, fielded jointly by BJP NCP and Shiv Sena . Dhiraj is the son of former chief minister Vilasrao Deshmukh.At the centre of the rift is cooperation minister and NCP member Babasaheb Patil, who broke ranks with the alliance and backed the Congress panel. In Oct, Patil rejected Mahayuti’s plan for a united contest, saying, “I had a 40-year association with the Congress panel. Moreover, cooperative elections are not fought on party symbols.”Patil later attended the nomination filing of Congress-panel candidate Avinash Patil from the Ahmedpur society constituency, making his stand public.BJP responded sharply. Former minister Sambhaji Patil Nilangekar alleged that Patil had aligned with Dhiraj Deshmukh and raised the issue with NCP leadership, seeking action against the minister. The controversy put Mahayuti’s unity under scrutiny, with the state’s cooperation minister openly campaigning against the alliance’s own panel.In an attempt to contain the fallout, Mahayuti members launched Parivartan Panel in Nov.BJP MLC Baswaraj Patil, Nilangekar, MLAs Sanjay Bansode and Ramesh Karad, and former minister Vinayakrao Patil attended the event, accusing the bank of benefiting a particular family instead of farmers.Sahakar Panel has highlighted its performance record, citing annual profits of over Rs 100 crore, crop loans worth Rs 1,780 crore, net profits of Rs 249 crore, recruitment of 263 local youths and 13 awards. It has promised new branches in every taluka, interest-free marriage loans, education loans and full computerisation.Parivartan Panel has challenged several of those claims, particularly on interest-free farmer loans, and positioned itself as an alternative focused on farmers’ interests.The election will determine control of a key cooperative institution in drought-prone Latur and test whether Mahayuti can maintain local cohesion after one of its own ministers sided with the opposition. A total of 999 voters will elect 19 directors. Thirty candidates are in the fray, while four have already been elected unopposed.
Article Summary: The election to Latur District Central Cooperative Bank on Sunday has emerged as the clearest public sign yet of cracks within Mahayuti. At the centre of the rift is cooperation minister and NCP member Babasaheb Patil, who broke ranks with the alliance and backed the Congress panel. Thirty candidates are in the fray, while four have already been elected unopposed.

Police are checking the CCTV cameras along the route to identify the vehicle and its owner.The accident took place after 3.30 am. The injured was rushed to Miraj Govt Hospital, but was declared dead by the doctors.The highway stretch sees speeding vehicles. Four years ago, an SUV rammed into a Warkari dindi at Junoni, a few kilometres from Bhose Phata, killing seven people.

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:

NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Article Title: Rs3 lakh stolen from farmer’s parked car in Chinchwad; driver suspected
Article Text:
Representative image

Pune:





A 20-year-old driver allegedly stole Rs3 lakh from his employer’s parked car in the early hours of Nov 6 in Chinchwad.The farmer (47), a resident of Chinchwad, lodged a complaint with Chinchwad police on Friday.An officer from Chinchwad police said the complainant owns a farm in Saswad in Purandar taluka. He had sold custard apples to a trader in the Saswad market. On Nov 5, the farmer and his driver went to meet the trader and collected Rs3 lakh from him. The farmer kept the cash in the glove box of his car.After reaching home, the driver parked the car in the farmer’s goods storage near his residence and forgot to take the cash with him. “The next day, the driver’s cellphone was switched off. The farmer went to the driver’s room but he was not there. The farmer took the car keys to check the vehicle and found the cash missing,” the officer said.“The CCTV footage showed the driver getting into the car and leaving after some time. The driver is from Raebareli in Uttar Pradesh. We are searching for him,” the officer said.

Article Title: 2 TN cops take 5.5 lakh bribe to file false Pocso case, suspended
Article Text:
Inspector Vijayalakshmi and constable Vasantharaja faced suspension after being caught in a bribery scandal

Accused 'arranged' complaint to take revenge on the woman

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





CHENNAI: A police inspector and a constable were suspended on Sunday for accepting 5 lakh bribe to frame a young man in a Pocso case. Police said a matrimonial fraud suspect had engineered the complaint after the man's sister rejected his marriage proposal.Inspector Vijayalakshmi and constable Vasantharaja, attached to the Thirumangalam All Women Police Station, were suspended after a preliminary inquiry. The conspiracy emerged when police were questioning Suresh Kanna, a Telangana native, arrested in another case related to matrimonial fraud in Neyveli.Police said Kanna had approached a Chennai woman through a matrimonial website, claiming to be 25 years old. When she grew suspicious and rejected his proposal, he allegedly arranged to implicate her younger brother in a criminal case.Through intermediaries, Kanna arranged for a 17-year-old girl to befriend the woman's younger brother online.They were in touch for nearly three months. On Aug 23, she invited him to a mall in Thirumangalam, police said. She later lodged a complaint alleging he had sexually harassed her at the mall and attempted to assault her near the parking area.Based on her statement, Vijayalakshmi registered a case against the woman's brother under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (Pocso) Act. However, before police could arrest Sriram, a video purportedly showing the complainant arguing with another girl on a road while intoxicated surfaced online. Police deferred the arrest.Meanwhile, Suresh Kanna was arrested by the Neyveli police in connection with a matrimonial fraud case. During interrogation, Kanna told police that he had 'arranged' the complaint to take revenge on the Chennai woman.He said he paid 5 lakh through intermediaries for her brother's arrest and claimed that police had not arrested him despite the payment.Senior police officers said they are examining the circumstances under which the Pocso case was registered and the alleged involvement of police personnel.
Article Summary: Inspector Vijayalakshmi and constable Vasantharaja were suspended after a preliminary inquiry. The conspiracy emerged when police were questioning Suresh Kanna, a Telangana native, arrested in another case related to matrimonial fraud in Neyveli.

Article Title: HC directs state to provide mosquito nets to all wards in GRH in six months
Article Text:
HC directs state to provide mosquito nets to all wards in GRH in six months

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





Madurai: Madras high court has directed the state to ensure that all wards in Govt Rajaji Hospital (GRH) in Madurai are provided with mosquito nets within six months.A division bench of Justice P Velmurugan and Justice K K Ramakrishnan was hearing a public interest litigation filed by A V Kathir of Madurai seeking a direction to the authorities for procurement of equipment for the cardiology department at GRH.The bench observed that the petitioner is a student pursuing his collegiate education in Bengaluru and is presently residing outside Tamil Nadu. The court is of the considered opinion that he is not entitled to maintain the present public interest litigation. Accordingly, the petition was liable to be dismissed on the ground of locus standi, the judges observed.However, considering the larger public interest involved in the matter, particularly with regard to the facilities and amenities available at GRH, the court is inclined to issue certain directions to the authorities, the judges observed. Taking into account the official submissions, the judges directed the authorities to ensure that all the wards of GRH are provided with mosquito nets within six months and file a compliance report before the court.The judges further directed the authorities to submit a detailed report within 15 days on the medical equipment and other essential amenities required for the effective functioning of GRH and the equipment and amenities already available at the hospital. The court adjourned the case to Dec 4 for filing the report.
Article Summary: Madras high court has directed the state to ensure that all wards in Govt Rajaji Hospital (GRH) in Madurai are provided with mosquito nets within six months. The judges further directed the authorities to submit a detailed report within 15 days on the medical equipment and other essential amenities required for the effective functioning of GRH.

Article Title: Temple should be allowed to light Karthigai deepam at deepathoon: BJP
Article Text:
Thiruparankundram hill

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





Madurai: BJP Tamil Nadu chief spokesperson Narayanan Thirupathy has said that the temple should be allowed to light Karthigai deepam at the deepathoon atop Thiruparankundram hill without further obstruction in line with Madras high court ’s directions.In a statement, he said the state govt’s counter-affidavit before Supreme Court on Nov 12, opposing the plea for ASI involvement and permanent lighting of Karthigai deepam at the deepathoon, was unnecessary and seeks to reopen issues already settled by Madras HC. In Dec 2025, Justice G R Swaminathan directed the temple management to light the deepam at the deepathoon. The order was confirmed by a division bench in Jan 2026. The state itself filed an SLP against them only on June 11, on which Supreme Court issued notice but refused to stay the high court directions.He said the fresh counter affidavit continues to rely on the older 1996 directions, insists that the deepathoon is not a traditional site, and resists any meaningful ASI role beyond limited protection of the cave and inscriptions. This directly contradicts the specific and later findings of the high court, which already recognised ASI’s protective role over the hill.He said the TVK govt appears to be following the same approach earlier followed by DMK, prioritising minority vote banks even when it means obstructing the majority’s long-standing religious practices on temple-owned land. There is nothing wrong with protecting minority rights or ensuring communal harmony. However, that cannot be done by repeatedly hurting the religious sentiments of the majority and denying a temple the right to perform its rituals on its own property, he added.
Article Summary: BJP Tamil Nadu chief spokesperson Narayanan Thirupathy has said that the temple should be allowed to light Karthigai deepam at the deepathoon. He said the state govt’s counter-affidavit before Supreme Court on Nov 12 was unnecessary and seeks to reopen issues already settled by Madras HC.

Article Title: Dosa shop turns into battleground: 2 women throw food items, vandalise outlet in Varanasi
Article Text:

VARANASI: Two women created a ruckus at a popular dosa outlet on Mahmoorganj Road, under the Bhelupur police station area on Saturday evening, allegedly vandalising the shop after its owner refused to pay extortion money.ACP (Bhelupur) Gaurav Kumar said that, based on a complaint filed by the shop owner, Bhelupur police registered an FIR against two unidentified women under Sections 324(4) (causing property damage), 115(2) (voluntarily causing hurt), 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke a breach of peace) and 351(3) (aggravated criminal intimidation) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). A detailed investigation into the case was underway, he added.The incident took place around 8.30pm on Saturday at a popular dosa outlet on Mahmoorganj Road. In his complaint, the shop owner, Bal Mukund, stated that two women arrived on a black scooter and allegedly demanded extortion money. When the employees refused to comply, the women entered the outlet and began throwing items from the counter onto the road.The complaint further alleged that the women assaulted employees and customers who tried to intervene.A child accompanying one of the customers was reportedly injured during the chaos. The owner also claimed that the women attempted to take cash from the counter before leaving and threatened to kill the staff and implicate them in false cases.The incident was captured on the shop's CCTV cameras. The viral footage showed one of the women recording a video while claiming that the shop owner and his staff had beaten up their father. Meanwhile, the other woman was seen throwing raw dosa ingredients and food items onto the road and at the cook before entering the shop.When some customers objected to the women's actions, the duo allegedly got into an argument with them.
Article Summary: The incident took place around 8.30pm on Saturday at a popular dosa outlet on Mahmoorganj Road. Bhelupur police registered an FIR against two unidentified women. The incident was captured on the shop's CCTV cameras.
